basis: Dystonia defines neurologic involvement; Ringbinden are structural abnormalities of skeletal muscle fibers.
Inherited dystonia; neurologic manifestations predominate. Pes cavus occurs in only 1/12.
Thyrotropin-producing anterior pituitary neoplasm; endocrine origin and hormone excess.
Breast carcinoma; breast has no axis. Metastatic sites are not inherent organ labels.
Malignant tumor arising in the peritoneum, assigned to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital lower-lip abnormality with dental abnormalities; lip and dentition belong to the oral gastrointestinal axis.
Joubert neurodevelopmental disorder with retinal dystrophy in 4/4; finger contractures in 2/4 support musculoskeletal involvement. Renal and cardiac defects each 1/8.
Alopecia, failed tooth eruption and ocular abnormalities define GAPO; skeletal maturation delay and joint hypermobility occur in 80-99%.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability characterize the broad 16q deletion group; other organ defects vary by deleted interval.
Biotin-dependent metabolic defects; neurologic dysfunction and dermatitis/alopecia are common, roughly >=30% in symptomatic multiple carboxylase deficiency.
Benign neoplasm originating in breast tissue; breast has no axis.
Umbrella for immune and infectious consequences of transplantation, including GVHD and engraftment syndrome; no damaged organ is consistent across the group.
Benign neoplasm arising in the cerebellum.
Nephronophthisis is the established core phenotype; retinal, CNS and respiratory disease vary, with group-wide frequencies insufficiently established.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with progressive visual loss.
Cutis laxa with skeletal defects and glycosylation abnormality; developmental delay/microcephaly in 80-99%. Common dental abnormalities omitted at cap; VSD evidence limited to 1 patient.
Distal skeletal myopathy with rimmed vacuoles, atrophy and myopathic EMG; facial weakness does not establish peripheral nerve disease.
Congenital immunodeficiency with defining polyclonal B-cell expansion and splenomegaly; recurrent infections do not establish lasting lung or ear damage.
Tumor occupying the spinal epidural space, commonly compressing spinal neural structures; vascularity does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Marrow failure, nail/skin changes and oral leukoplakia define disease; reduced DLCO in 4/12 supports pulmonary damage. Bone findings omitted at cap; epiphora alone insufficient.
Severe neurodevelopmental disorder; optic atrophy in 1/2 supports direct ocular damage, although the reported sample is very small.
Premature ovarian insufficiency is failure of gonadal endocrine function, beyond infertility alone.
Tumor of the frontal sinus; paranasal sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis. Lymphoma is only one possible subtype.
Locally aggressive tumor arising in bone; definition establishes bone origin despite the malignant parent classification.
Lung injury from aspirated or inhaled oils or fats; chemical pneumonitis does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease.
